extracted.intended_audience: Offshore project developers/lessees, engineers, and project verification agents preparing and submitting GAPs, SAPs, COPs, FDRs, FIRs, CVA nominations, and related reports to BOEM
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and report content standards for submitting GOM/OCS GAPs, SAPs, COPs, Facility Design Reports, Fabrication & Installation Reports, CVA nominations, and related verification/recordkeeping to BOEM. Covers information that must be included, CVA roles, inspection and reporting expectations, and BOEM review/processing timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategy for compliance with §§585.705–585.714
rubrics_metrics.description: If your project supports a complex or significant determination, describe your strategy for compliance with §§585.705 through 585.714.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a plan showing how you will meet CVA, verification, inspection, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements when BOEM deems the project complex or significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information incorporated by reference
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of the documents you have incorporated by reference and where they may be publicly accessed; for confidential information, you may reference information and data discussed in other plans previously submitted or that are otherwise readily available to BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify each referenced document and public access location; for confidential material, reference prior submissions or BOEM-available data instead of resubmitting confidential attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other information as required by BOEM
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information as required by BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may request project-specific supplemental data; include a placeholder or commitment to supply other information on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological and geotechnical reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports to define baseline geological conditions, provide data to develop a geologic model, assess geologic hazards, and determine feasibility of the proposed facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include desktop studies, geophysical surveys (sufficient areal coverage, depth penetration, resolution), geotechnical investigations to ground-truth geophysics and support preliminary foundation design, and an integrated site characterization report with geological model, supporting data, findings, and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological survey reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Description of biological surveys used to determine presence of live bottoms, hard bottoms, topographic features, and marine resources including migratory populations (fish, marine mammals, sea turtles, sea birds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide survey methods, results, and interpretation relevant to project siting and impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archaeological resources and other historic property surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: Archaeological resource and other historic property identification surveys with supporting data to provide BOEM required information under NHPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include survey methodologies, findings, maps, and supporting data sufficient for BOEM NHPA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteorological and oceanographic (metocean) reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports to provide an overall understanding of meteorological and oceanographic conditions at the site and identify conditions posing significant risk to the facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include desktop studies using hindcast/re-analysis models and field measurements in sufficient detail to support preliminary facility design and analyses of wake effects, sediment mobility/scour, and navigation risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional information for project easements or complex/significant facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If applying for a project easement, or constructing a facility or combination of facilities deemed complex or significant by BOEM, provide additional information and comply with subpart H requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect to supply extended construction, cable/pipeline, operational, schedule, and other technical information as described in subpart H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and operation concept
rubrics_metrics.description: A discussion of the objectives, description of the proposed activities, and tentative schedule from start to completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear project objectives, activity descriptions, and a reasonable timeline showing milestones from start to finish.

rubrics_metrics.name: All cables and pipelines (including project easement cables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the location, design, installation methods, testing, maintenance, repair, safety devices, exterior corrosion protection, inspections, and decommissioning for all cables and pipelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include technical drawings, burial methods, protection measures, inspection regimes, and lifecycle/decommissioning plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating procedures and systems
rubrics_metrics.description: A general description of operating procedures and systems under normal conditions and in case of accidents or emergencies (natural or manmade).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe routine operations and emergency response measures, including roles, procedures, and interfaces with safety systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: A reasonable schedule of construction activity showing significant milestones leading to commencement of activities consistent with subpart H requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide milestone dates, phasing, and dependencies sufficient for BOEM technical and environmental review.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA and other-law supporting information with GAP (§585.646)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit, with your GAP, detailed information and analysis to assist BOEM in complying with NEPA and other applicable laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide topic-specific analyses and data (see enumerated topics) to support BOEM's environmental and legal reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Water quality analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Address turbidity and total suspended solids from construction; impact from vessel discharges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe anticipated construction-related turbidity, TSS, and vessel discharge impacts and mitigation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitive biological resources or habitats
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify essential fish habitat, refuges, preserves, special management areas in coastal management programs, marine protected areas (State and Federal), nearby national marine sanctuaries/monuments, rookeries, hard bottom habitat, chemosynthetic communities, calving grounds, barrier islands, beaches, dunes, and wetlands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map and describe nearby protected resources and analyze potential impacts and avoidance/minimization measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archaeological, Indigenous, and treaty/reserved rights uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information on archaeological resources, other historic property use, Indigenous traditional cultural use, or use pertaining to treaty and reserved rights with Native Americans or other Indigenous peoples to support NHPA or other laws/policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include identification surveys, consultation results, and documentation needed for BOEM's NHPA and treaty-rights analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and economic conditions analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Address employment, existing offshore/coastal infrastructure, land use, subsistence resources and harvest practices, recreation, recreational/commercial fishing (typical seasons, location, type), minority and lower income groups, coastal zone management programs, and a visual impact assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide socioeconomic baseline data and assess potential impacts on communities, fisheries, and coastal uses; include visual impact assessment methods and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coastal and marine uses and navigational safety risk assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify military activities, vessel traffic, fisheries, and exploration/development of other resources; include a navigational safety risk assessment describing predicted impacts to navigation and measures to avoid or minimize adverse impacts. Submit this document to U.S. Coast Guard if potential impediments to safe navigation are identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide vessel traffic analyses, conflict mapping, proposed mitigation, and coordination with USCG for navigational safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coastal Zone Management Act (CZMA) consistency certification
rubrics_metrics.description: If required by CZMA, include a Consistency Certification under 15 CFR part 930 subpart D (if GAP submitted before lease/grant issuance) or subpart E (if after issuance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submission to applicable State CZMA agencies per the appropriate subpart and provide required supporting data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal consistency processing for GAP (§585.647)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before lease/grant issuance, furnish GAP, consistency certification, and necessary data to State CZMA agencies per 15 CFR part 930 subpart D and submit a copy to BOEM per §585.110; after issuance, submit under subpart E and BOEM will forward to State agencies after BOEM determines information requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the timing and routing rules for CZMA consistency review; ensure copies to BOEM and State agencies as prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM review to determine sufficiency (§585.648)
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM will review your submitted GAP and associated information and certifications to determine if it contains information necessary to conduct technical and environmental reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comprehensive information up-front to avoid deficiency notices and delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM disapproval and revision opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM disapproves your GAP, BOEM will inform you of the reasons and allow an opportunity to submit a revised plan addressing concerns; BOEM may suspend your lease or grant as appropriate to allow resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to respond to objection letters and revise plans; suspension of lease/grant is possible until issues are resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to conduct activities under approved GAP (§585.652)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a limited lease, time period established under §585.236(a)(2), unless BOEM renews the term under §§585.425–585.429.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check applicable lease term rules to determine authorized activity timeframe.

rubrics_metrics.name: When GAP revisions are required (§585.655)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must notify BOEM in writing before conducting any activities not described in your approved GAP, describing the proposed activities; BOEM will determine if authorized or require a revision, may request additional information, and will determine if revised GAP is complex/significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify BOEM in advance of changes; BOEM may require compliance with §585.650 or §585.651 depending on complexity determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of activities likely requiring GAP revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Activities likely to require a proposed revision include: activities not described in your approved GAP; modifications to number, size, or type of facilities/equipment; changes in geographic location/layout beyond described ranges; structural failure of any facility; or change to any activity specified by BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this list to assess whether a proposed change triggers formal revision and prior BOEM approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decommissioning after completion (§585.657)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion of approved activities under your GAP, you must decommission your project as set forth in subpart J.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include decommissioning planning and compliance with subpart J requirements in project lifecycle planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air quality requirements in SAP/COP/GAP (§585.659)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your SAP, COP, or GAP must address air quality; in the western Gulf of Mexico (west of 87.5° W) and offshore North Slope Borough of Alaska include any information required for BOEM to make air quality determinations and submit three copies of the modeling report and three sets of digital files as supporting information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide modeled emissions, monitoring, control measures, and submit required hardcopy and digital modeling deliverables where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports required before installing facilities (§585.700)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a Facility Design Report (FDR) and a Fabrication and Installation Report (FIR) before installing facilities described in your approved SAP, COP, or GAP (when required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may submit separate FDRs/FIRs for major components by agreement with BOEM, but must explain integration and demonstrate verification by a CVA if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate FDRs/FIRs and integration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitting separate FDRs and FIRs for major components, explain how all components will function together effectively in an integrated manner and demonstrate integration has been verified by your CVA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide system-level integration analysis and CVA verification statements when breaking reports into component-level documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commencement conditions for fabrication/installation
rubrics_metrics.description: You may commence fabrication and installation on the OCS described in each report if BOEM deems the report submitted and notifies non-objection or does not respond with objections within 60 calendar days of SAP/COP/GAP approval or of the report being deemed submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track BOEM 60-calendar-day review windows; do not commence activities subject to objections until objections are resolved to BOEM's satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement/fabrication allowed prior to reports
rubrics_metrics.description: You may commence procurement of commercially available standardized parts and fabrication activities not on the OCS (e.g., manufacturing) prior to submittal of required reports, subject to CVA verification; BOEM may object to installation if components or fabrication are inconsistent with standards, approved plans, FDR/FIR, or BOEM regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit pre-approval procurement to standardized/type-certified items and ensure CVA verification and documentation to minimize BOEM objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM objections and additional information timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If BOEM requires additional information or has objections, BOEM will notify you in writing within 60 calendar days of the report being deemed submitted. Following notification, BOEM may provide detailed objections; you cannot commence fabrication/installation activities addressed in those reports until you resolve all objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to deficiency notices; until objections cleared, activities governed by the reports cannot proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Cover letter content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letter must include proposed facility designations; lease, ROW or RUE grant number; area name and block numbers; and the type of facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide administrative identifiers and basic project designation information required for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Location plat requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Location plat must include latitude/longitude, UTM coordinates, state plane coordinates in Lambert or Transverse Mercator Projection, distances from nearest block lines, based on NAD 83; and location of any project easements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide geodetic coordinates in specified datums/projection systems and mapping of easement areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Front, side, and plan view drawing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must show facility dimensions and orientation, elevations relative to Mean Lower Low Water, and pile sizes and penetration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide engineering drawings with sufficient detail for structural and siting review.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Complete set of structural drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit approved-for-construction fabrication drawings including cathodic protection systems, jacket design, pile foundations, mooring/tethering systems, foundations/anchoring systems, and associated cable and pipeline designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide construction-level drawings for all structural components and associated systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Summary of environmental data used for design
rubrics_metrics.description: A summary of environmental data used in design or analysis (e.g., extreme weather, seafloor conditions, waves, wind, current, tides, temperature, snow/ice effects, marine growth, water depth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie environmental baselines to design criteria and loading assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Summary of engineering design data
rubrics_metrics.description: Loading information (live, dead, environmental); structural information (design-life, material types, cathodic protection, design criteria, fatigue life, jacket/deck/production component design, foundation pilings/templates, mooring/tethering systems, fabrication/installation guidelines); locations of foundation boreholes/piles; foundation information (soil stability, design criteria); and for floating facilities, integrity, stability, and ballast information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide engineering assumptions, load cases, design basis, and foundation/geotechnical interfaces used for design.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Complete set of design calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit all design calculations supporting the facility design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include structural, hydrodynamic, geotechnical, and fatigue calculations with supporting inputs and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Project-specific studies
rubrics_metrics.description: All studies pertinent to facility design or installation (e.g., oceanographic and soil reports, including required survey results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate referenced studies and survey outputs used in design decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Description of loads imposed on the facility
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe loads imposed by the jacket, decks, production components, foundations/piles/templates/anchoring systems, and mooring/tethering systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify and document load sources and design load cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Geotechnical and geophysical reports
rubrics_metrics.description: All data from geotechnical/geophysical surveys, in situ explorations, lab tests, analyses, burial/drivability assessments, and recommended design parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide raw data, interpreted results, and recommended design values for foundation design.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Archaeological resources reports
rubrics_metrics.description: All archaeological resource and historic property identification surveys with supporting data that BOEM has authorized you to submit with your FDR under §585.626(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach BOEM-authorized cultural resources reports and supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Design standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The industry standards you will apply to ensure the facilities are designed to meet §585.105.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List applicable codes/standards and justify their use relative to BOEM requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Critical Safety System risk assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A risk assessment that identifies the critical safety systems and description of the identified critical safety systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify, describe, and evaluate risk for systems deemed critical to safety; include commissioning and verification plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR — Other information
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information required by BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any BOEM-requested or project-specific data not captured elsewhere in the FDR checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR submission location (§585.701(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit your Facility Design Report to BOEM pursuant to §585.110.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §585.110 procedures for electronic or hardcopy submission as specified by BOEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDR CVA verification statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are required to use a CVA, the FDR must include the CVA verification statement: 'The design of this structure has been verified by a BOEM-approved CVA to be in accordance with accepted engineering practices and the approved SAP, GAP, or COP, as applicable, and has been designed to provide for safety. The verified design and as-built plans and specifications will be on file at [provide location].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert the exact CVA verification statement and provide location of verified design/as-built records.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIR — Cover letter and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: FIR cover letter must include proposed facility designation and identifiers; FIR must include fabrication and installation schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide administrative identifiers and a detailed timeline of fabrication and installation activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIR — Fabrication information and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The industry standards you will use to ensure the facilities are fabricated to the design criteria in your FDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State recognized fabrication standards and QA measures; alternate QA must be approved case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIR — Installation process information
rubrics_metrics.description: Details associated with deployment activities, equipment, materials, onshore/offshore equipment and support, and anchoring and mooring patterns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide step-by-step installation methods, equipment lists, vessel support, and anchoring/mode-of-installation diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIR — Permits
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal, State, and local permits (e.g., EPA, Army Corps) — include one copy or status of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach permit documents or application status summaries for required authorizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIR — Quality assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificates ensuring adherence to a recognized quality assurance standard; alternate means of compliance must be approved case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide QA certificates and procedures; seek alternate compliance approval if not using recognized standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIR — Environmental information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on water discharge, waste disposal, vessel information, onshore waste receiving/treatment/disposal facilities; may incorporate by reference if submitted in SAP/COP/GAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize environmental management plans and reference previously submitted environmental data where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIR — Commissioning procedures for critical safety systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Original equipment manufacturer procedures or other BOEM-approved procedures for commissioning of critical safety systems identified in §585.701(a)(13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide stepwise commissioning protocols, acceptance criteria, test procedures, and recordkeeping plans for critical safety systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIR — Project easement information
rubrics_metrics.description: Design of any cables, pipelines, or facilities, including burial methods and vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed designs and installation methods for easement-related infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIR — Other information
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional information required by BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide any BOEM-requested content not otherwise specified in FIR requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIR submission and project easement request (§585.702)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit your FIR to BOEM pursuant to §585.110; you may request any project easement and supporting information as part of your original FIR submission or as a revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: File FIRs per §585.110 and include easement requests if desired; ensure supporting data accompanies easement requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIR CVA verification statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If required to use a CVA, the FIR must include the CVA verification statement: 'The fabrication and installation of this structure has been verified by a BOEM-approved CVA to be in accordance with accepted engineering practices, the FDR, and the approved SAP, GAP, or COP, as applicable. The verified design and as-built plans and specifications will be on file at [provide location].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert exact CVA verification statement and reference location of verified as-built records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports for project modifications and repairs (§585.703)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must demonstrate in a report that major repairs and major modifications to a completed project conform to accepted engineering practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare engineering analyses and documentation showing repairs/modifications meet accepted practices and design criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'major repair' and 'major modification'
rubrics_metrics.description: Major repair: corrective action involving structural members affecting structural integrity or substantial repair of a critical safety system(s). Major modification: alteration involving structural members affecting structural integrity or substantial alteration of a critical safety system(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to determine whether proposed works trigger the major repair/modification reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: CVA verification required for modifications/repairs
rubrics_metrics.description: If required to use a CVA, the report for modifications/repairs must include a CVA verification statement that the work has been verified to be in accordance with accepted engineering practices, the FDR, and the approved SAP/GAP/COP as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the prescribed CVA verification text and supporting verification documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM actions after receiving FDR/FIR/project verification reports (§585.704)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 20 calendar days BOEM will review and deem reports submitted if sufficiently complete and accurate; if not, BOEM will notify you of problems/deficiencies within 20 days and will not deem the report submitted until corrections are made; BOEM will notify when deemed submitted; if BOEM does not notify within 20 days that there are problems, you may consider it deemed submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare complete submissions to meet the 20-day sufficiency check; respond promptly to deficiency notices to achieve 'deemed submitted' status.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use a Certified Verification Agent (CVA) (§585.705)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless BOEM waives the requirement, you must use one or more CVAs to review and verify your FDRs, FIRs, and Project Modification and Repair Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for CVA engagement unless you successfully petition for a waiver under the criteria provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of a CVA
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure facilities are designed, fabricated, and installed in conformance with accepted engineering practices and the FDR/FIR; ensure critical safety systems are commissioned per procedures; ensure major repairs/modifications conform to accepted practices; and provide BOEM and you with immediate reports of incidents affecting design/fabrication/installation/commissioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CVA responsibilities cover verification, monitoring, incident reporting, and assurance of conformance to accepted engineering practices and QA standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions under which BOEM may waive CVA requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may waive CVA in whole or part if you demonstrate: (1) design conforms to a standard design used successfully in similar environment and installation design conforms to accepted practices; (2) fabricator has successfully fabricated similar facilities and will fabricate in conformance with accepted practices and recognized QA standard; (3) installation companies have successfully installed similar facilities in similar environment and will install in conformance with accepted practices; (4) major repairs/modifications will be completed in conformance with accepted engineering practices and recognized QA standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence of prior successful use, QA controls, and similarity to justify waiver. Alternate QA means require case-by-case approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: CVA waiver request and appeal process
rubrics_metrics.description: You must submit a request to waive (in whole or part) the CVA requirement in writing; BOEM will review and notify decision; if BOEM does not waive, you may appeal under §585.118; if BOEM waives, your project engineer must perform CVA duties except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the written request process and be prepared to appeal denial or to have project engineer assume CVA roles if waiver granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: CVA nomination and approval (§585.706)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CVA must be nominated and approved by BOEM before conducting verification activities; if using multiple CVAs, nominate a general project CVA to manage verification strategy and ensure consistency; general project CVA must be nominated no later than COP submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit CVA nominations with required supporting information prior to verification activities and early enough to meet COP deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: CVA nomination content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Nomination must include technical capabilities of the individual or primary staff for the project, including relevant professional licenses, certifications, accreditations, and the scope and level of work to be performed by the CVA, including all relevant reports and facilities the CVA will verify.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document personnel qualifications, experience, licenses, and a clear scope-of-work for the CVA role.

rubrics_metrics.name: CVA conflict-of-interest prohibition and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals/organizations acting as CVAs must not function in any capacity creating a conflict or appearance of conflict (must not have prepared or been directly involved in original work they verify); verification must be conducted by or under direct supervision of a registered professional engineer; BOEM will approve or disapprove the CVA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure CVA independence and that PE-level oversight is documented; expect BOEM review and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: CVA duties for facility design review (§585.707)
rubrics_metrics.description: CVA must verify to BOEM that the facility is designed to withstand environmental and functional load conditions appropriate for intended service life at the proposed location and has been designed to provide for safety. Duties include design for human safety and accident prevention and, for floating facilities, structural integrity, stability, and ballast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CVA design review focuses on load-resistance, safety-focused design, human-safety considerations, and floating-specific stability assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: CVA/project engineer duties for fabrication & installation review (§585.708)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use good engineering judgment to independently assess fabrication/installation and commissioning; monitor fabrication/installation and commissioning as required; verify in a report that components are fabricated/installed in accordance with accepted engineering practices and recognized QA standard or equivalent, approved SAP/COP/GAP, and FIR; identify location of fabrication/installation records; provide records documenting commissioning of critical safety systems; identify location of commissioning records; and if multiple CVAs are involved the general project CVA must submit final project verification report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CVA must submit verifications allowing commencement of operations 30 days after BOEM receives the verification report unless BOEM objects; ensure traceable records and documentation for BOEM review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring changes and notification obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the CVA/project engineer finds fabrication/installation procedures or safety-system commissioning procedures changed or design specifications modified, the CVA must inform you; if you accept modifications, you must inform BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document deviations and change acceptances and promptly notify BOEM of any accepted modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onsite fabrication inspection verification items (§585.709)
rubrics_metrics.description: During fabrication, CVA/project engineer must periodically inspect and verify items as appropriate: quality control by lessee/builder; fabrication site facilities; material quality and identification methods; adherence to fabrication procedures specified in FIRs; welder and welding procedure qualification and identification; structural tolerances and adherence; nondestructive examination requirements and results; destructive testing requirements and results; repair procedures; installation of corrosion-protection and splash-zone protection; erection procedures to prevent overstressing; alignment procedures; dimensional checks of overall structure (including turrets, interfaces, mooring and chain, riser tensioning); and status of quality-control records at various fabrication stages. For floating facilities, verify structural integrity, stability, and ballast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform periodic in-person inspections, verify QA records and NDE/test results, and check weld and fabrication qualifications; document findings for BOEM and the final verification report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Onsite installation inspection duties (§585.710)
rubrics_metrics.description: CVA/project engineer must make periodic onsite inspections while installation is in progress and verify/witness/survey/check as appropriate: loadout and initial flotation; towing operations and towing records; launching and uprighting activities; submergence activities; pile or anchor installations; installation of mooring/tethering systems; final deck and component installations; installation at locations set forth in FDRs/FIRs; and commissioning of critical safety systems. For fixed/floating facilities verify proper procedures for loadout, actual installation, and commissioning; for floating facilities verify loadout, installation of foundation pilings/templates/anchoring systems, and installation of mooring/tethering systems. Conduct onsite inspection of the installed facility, make periodic inspections witnessing commissioning to verify systems function as designed and that final commissioning records are complete, and spot-check equipment/procedures/recordkeeping to determine compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witness critical marine operations, verify records, and document commissioning outcomes and any nonconformances.

rubrics_metrics.name: CVA/project engineer reporting requirements (§585.712)
rubrics_metrics.description: CVA/project engineer must prepare and submit to you and BOEM all reports and records required by this subpart, submit interim reports as requested by BOEM, and submit final reports to BOEM pursuant to §585.110. For each report include summarization of any issues with the design and any incidents during fabrication/installation or commissioning and how those issues were resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely interim and final reports with clear summaries of incidents, nonconformances, corrective actions, and locations of records; follow BOEM submittal procedures in §585.110.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records to be kept relating to FDRs, FIRs, and modification/repair reports (§585.714)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must keep records relating to FDRs, FIRs, and Project Modification and Repair Reports, including the records of the commissioning of critical safety systems. You must provide BOEM with the location of these records in the certification statement as required in §§585.701(c), 585.703(b), and 585.708(a)(5)(i) and (a)(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain accessible, auditable repositories for verification and provide location information in required certification statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Management System (SMS) requirement (§585.810)
rubrics_metrics.description: You are required to use a Safety Management System (SMS) for activities conducted on the OCS to develop or operate a lease (from met buoy placement and site assessment through decommissioning) and to provide your SMS to BOEM upon request. You must also submit a detailed description of the SMS with your COP and, when required by this part, your SAP or GAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop an SMS covering lifecycle activities, document procedures, roles, and controls, and include detailed SMS description as part of COP (and SAP/GAP when required).
